videos.script: A report is not the end of a defect. It is the start of a short life. {{life}} Somebody reads it and decides whether it is real, and how soon it matters. {{triage}} A developer fixes it. A new build arrives. And you, the tester, run it again. {{retest}} If it passes, the defect is closed. If it fails, it comes back to the developer, reopened. {{reopen}} This lesson draws that life as a set of states and the moves between them. {{states}} Then it sits in a triage meeting on boxoffice 1.1, where seven open defects and three new reports wait for a decision. {{meeting}} One new report turns out to be a duplicate. Another turns out to be the requirement working as written. {{dup}} Last, the numbers. Some tell a team something true, like how long defects wait and how often a fix fails. Others are theatre, and they reward the wrong work. {{numbers}}
